summary.added_external_crate_count_note: P2-P2 admits no external crate. academic-deletion links academic-consent, academic-domain, academic-evidence-center, academic-proposal, academic-retention, academic-student-voice and thiserror as product edges, academic-vault as an optional product edge behind the non-default deletion-engine lane, and academic-crypto, academic-domain, academic-policy, academic-proposal, academic-retention, serde_json and trybuild as dev edges, all covered by earlier reviewed receipts, and adds one workspace path package. Nothing links into a product binary that was not already there: every workspace product edge is a path package this repository already builds, and thiserror was admitted by the phase 1 receipt. Build-time-only additions are zero -- there is no build script, no proc macro beyond serde's and thiserror's, and no code generator.
summary.added_workspace_path_package_note: academic-deletion is the P2-P2 boundary: the user-facing side of P2-K5. It owns the dry run, which carries one node per derivative class in registry order and has one constructor; the impact preview, which extends P2-G6's expiry preview through P2-L5's own projection walk to section 32.5's concept and evidence projections and refuses a citation map that does not cover every artifact the dry run reaches; the confirmation, which takes the preview by value and issues P2-M2's UserDecision so no automatic actor can produce one; the protection decision, whose refusing arm carries a policy reason and whose type has no boolean form; the provider erasure log, which links P2-G3's persisted deletion receipt to the artifact deletion that caused the request; the external leak incident, which advances only by section 34.4's four recovery steps and has no transition a claim supersession can drive; and the executor, which is the real implementation behind P2-K5's two seams. It is a separate package from academic-retention because that crate is the mechanism -- rotation, revocation, crypto-shredding and the result vocabulary -- and this one is the product flow around it, and because the direction of the edge is what keeps the mechanism linkable with no flow and the flow impossible without the mechanism.

no_second_vocabulary_note: The seven derivative classes are academic_retention::DerivativeClass, read through the product edge rather than restated: academic-consent already carries the one permitted copy, kept in step by the_two_derivative_vocabularies_are_the_same_list, and a third copy is what this crate's product edge exists to avoid. The four result words are academic_retention::RetentionOutcome and are decided by that crate's settle, so this crate re-derives neither COMPLETE nor PARTIAL nor REPAIR_REQUIRED; the unresolved rows it renders are built by that crate's own UnresolvedLocator::to_row, because UnresolvedReason is non_exhaustive and a second spelling would need a wildcard arm that turns a fifth reason into a row nobody can read. Section 32.5's two projection families are academic_student_voice::AffectedProjectionKind and the walk over them is that crate's affected_projections and unreferenced_objects, called and not forked -- P2-L5 answered section 32.5 for a lecture expiry and this crate asks the same question for an artifact deletion, so the two functions were made public there rather than copied here. The provider deletion receipt reference is academic_evidence_center::DeletionReceiptRef and the receipt state is that crate's ReceiptState, whose columns are already compared against academic-policy's DeletionReceiptRow; this crate adds the link to the deletion action and no second receipt shape. The non-delegable door is academic_proposal::UserDecision::by, which matches exhaustively over academic-domain's closed actor enum, so no second actor check is written here and a fifth actor variant stops that crate compiling rather than slipping past a negated list. The seven classes are checked against section 32.10's own sentence, parsed out of the design document and compared in both directions, and the four recovery steps against section 34.4's leak row the same way, so a count this crate states is the document's rather than one it remembers.

direct_workspace_dependencies.academic-consent: P2-G6's RetentionTerms vocabulary, named by the protection reason that refuses a deletion under a retention floor. Audio and transcript retention are two bounds there and a derivative inherits the stricter through that crate's one inheritance function; this crate declares no inheritance rule and no bound of its own.
direct_workspace_dependencies.academic-domain: ArtifactId, ContentDigest, EgressDecisionId, TimestampMillis and Actor. The artifact identity is the half a locator does not carry, and it is what every map in this crate is keyed by; the actor is what P2-M2's UserDecision::by refuses every non-user variant of.
direct_workspace_dependencies.academic-evidence-center: P2-X7's DeletionReceiptRef and ReceiptState, so the provider half of a deletion carries the correction centre's own record; and CorrectionRecord and CorrectionChoice, so leak_incident_cannot_be_closed_by_claim_supersession is a statement about two types that are both in scope rather than about one this crate invented. A leak incident records that a correction was filed and moves nowhere, which is section 34.6's fifth principle.
direct_workspace_dependencies.academic-proposal: P2-M2's UserDecision. It is issued only for Actor::User by an exhaustive match over a closed enum, so deletion_confirmation_is_non_delegable is that crate's door reused. P2-M4, the task that forces non-delegable actions generally, has not merged; this crate closes its own case with a type rather than waiting for it.
direct_workspace_dependencies.academic-retention: P2-K5's whole deletion contract: DerivativeClass and DERIVATIVE_CLASSES, ClassResolution and DerivativeResolver, DeletionPlan, PlannedAction and ActionKind, RetentionExecutor and settle, RetentionOutcome, UnresolvedLocator, UnresolvedReason and UnresolvedSet, AppendOnlyJournal and its deletion journal path, BackupTombstone and tombstone::write_into_backup. That crate's contract page says P2-P2 is the task that supplies the real implementations behind its resolver and executor seams, and this is that task. The edge selects no rotation-engine feature, so the default graph resolves the plan, the journal, the vocabulary and the tombstone -- all pure Rust -- and not the encrypted object namespace.
direct_workspace_dependencies.academic-student-voice: P2-L5's EvidenceIndex, ProjectionRecord, AffectedProjection, AffectedProjectionKind and ProjectionEffect, and the two walk functions affected_projections and unreferenced_objects. Section 32.5 asks that the impact of one deletion on concept and evidence projections be shown in advance, P2-L5 answered it for a lecture expiry, and calling that walk is what keeps one answer to one question.
direct_workspace_dependencies.academic-vault: Optional, and only the non-default deletion-engine lane selects it. EncryptedVault and its object header constants, for the shredder that destroys a real key slot through P2-K5's shred_with_tombstone and for the object-tree index behind it. Selecting the lane also selects academic-retention/rotation-engine, which is the only build in which this crate can open an object at all.

dev_workspace_dependencies.academic-crypto: The RB01 fixture's profile: VaultMasterKey, ProfileId, RecoverySecret and create_recovery_recipient, so the child process that is killed at the vault's key-slot failpoint reopens the same generation the parent sealed under, from the profile's own recipient record and a fixed synthetic secret rather than from a key handed across a process boundary.
dev_workspace_dependencies.academic-domain: Declared a second time for the trybuild reason academic-scenario and academic-evidence-center give: a compile-fail case compiles against this crate plus this crate's dev-dependencies, and two of the three cases name a TimestampMillis.
dev_workspace_dependencies.academic-policy: P2-G3's PermissionBroker, DeletionReceiptDraft and DeletionReceiptRow. provider_deletion_receipt_is_stored_and_linked drives the real broker -- registers a provider policy, installs a rule, evaluates a request, executes the capability, and stores the receipt against the grant and the exact allow-audit row -- and then links that stored row's own digests into this crate's erasure log. It stays a dev edge on purpose: a product closure holding the broker could name a type that owns a transmitted byte, and every_field_type_in_this_crate_is_reviewed rests on that closure not holding one.
dev_workspace_dependencies.academic-proposal: Declared a second time for the same trybuild reason.
dev_workspace_dependencies.academic-retention: Declared a second time for the same trybuild reason, and used by the fixtures for DERIVATIVE_CLASSES, the journal path and the tombstone reader.
dev_workspace_dependencies.serde_json: The RB01 fixture hands the sealed artifact's descriptor to the killed child as JSON. A child that re-derived the descriptor would be deriving it from the same code the parent used; reading the parent's own record is what makes the two processes agree on one artifact rather than on one procedure.
dev_workspace_dependencies.trybuild: The compile-fail suite. Two of this task's refusals are absent constructors and an absent conversion, and the three cases under crates/deletion/tests/compile_fail assert that each is a program that does not compile with a committed diagnostic -- a deletion confirmation written as a struct literal, an incident closure written as a struct literal, and a correction record converted into a closure or into the closed state.

why_this_dependency_belongs_inside_its_t: academic-deletion is the only crate in the workspace that composes a deletion: it reads what a deletion would reach, shows the user what it costs, takes a confirmation that only a user can give, and drives P2-K5's executor. Every one of those steps is a refusal that has to live in one place -- a preview that is not total, a confirmation from a model actor, a protected artifact refused without a reason, a receipt for a request nobody made, and a leak incident closed by a claim correction are five different failures with one owner. Splitting them across the crates that own each input would put the refusal beside the value rather than beside the decision, and the decision is what P2-P2 is. It links academic-retention because destroying a key slot is that crate's mechanism and this crate is the flow that decides when to; it does not link academic-store, so it holds no canonical writer and adds no migration; and it does not link academic-policy or academic-egress-boundary on the product edge, so no product file in it can name a type that owns a transmitted byte.
network_posture: No socket. The crate's link closure carries libc and nothing else, through academic-policy's bundled SQLite by way of academic-evidence-center's dependency on academic-ingestion; the crate itself spells no socket construct, opens no connection, and reads no clock or environment variable -- this_crate_reads_no_clock_and_no_environment compares the whole product source for both. The deletion-engine lane adds academic-vault, which is filesystem-only. Nothing here reaches a provider: a provider erasure request is a record of an identity and two instants, and the request itself is P2-G3's to make through the broker.
advisory_path: No new advisory surface. Every crate in the closure was admitted by an earlier receipt and is covered by the same cargo-deny and pnpm audit gates the phase 1 receipt names; this task adds no external crate, no build script, no proc macro and no npm package.
